items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...with letters from Gene Williams and other people about his activities.

ctx.x: I don't know anything about it. I think he finished it, and it was supposed to have been pretty good, but I don't know about the publication.

I never did know what happened to him. I know one funny thing that happened one day, he wanted to get Bunks' reaction to Jelly Rolls' Library of Congress records. He'd gotten a few of them that Lomax or somebody had given him tests, which Lomax really wasn't supposed to give out. I gave some later to Charles Smith and I, too, and then Spivak, the head of the department, found out about it and stopped it right in the middle of the series, or after we had about two-thirds. But anyway, one day he brought those up to…
Yeah, well, of course, when I moved up to New York, I think the Stuyvesant engagement was over already. That ended about the 10th or so. Well, this was the second.

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: I ran into Buckland Moon in New York recently whom I hadn't seen since the Stuyvesant days... I guess Gene was running it... I know he was quite active.

ctx.x: Do you have any impression of Gene Williams or something I wanted to ask you about?

Well, Gene was a... a very bright guy. His initial, uh... impact, I think, was that of a kind of very well-educated, very polite, and somewhat shy, I believe. At least this was the first impression. Uh... With, uh... a kind of a sense of humor. I mean, he seemed to be, as I remember him, always on the pleasant kidding side. Although, uh... He might have been too much on that. I mean, maybe, uh... Maybe he was one of these people that smiles all the time, uh... regardless of, uh... how they feel, but, uh... Uh...…
Well, there was a lot of this guy's hostility in this kidding?
